item.description:
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey has landed on digital platforms.
The move to digital comes exactly four months after the movie’s initial release in theaters, making it the longest theatrical window of 2026. Why would you rush the digital release for a movie that keeps selling out?
If you somehow didn’t catch the movie in theaters, or are already itching for the at-home rewatch, here’s where to find the movie on digital as well as all of the info we have about The Odyssey’s streaming and home entertainment releases.
The Odyssey Is Now Available on Digital
The Odyssey is now available to rent or purchase digitally (see at Prime Video). Choosing to purchase the movie will net you over 90 minutes of bonus features across 12 behind-the-scenes featurettes.
The Odyssey, which boasts a full runtime of almost three hours, is legendary director Christopher Nolan’s take on Ulysses’ epic. Matt Damon stars as Odysseus, while future Bond himself, Robert Pattinson, goes full weasel mode in the role of Antinous.
This is Nolan we’re talking about, so the movie can be aptly described as a full spectacle. The man is very dedicated to his special effects, which are in full display across The Odyssey’s mythology-inspired sequences.
IGN’s review goes so far as to call it a "must-watch cinematic experience," and audiences appear to have felt the same way. After multiple extensions, The Odyssey has grossed over $1.5 billion, making it second only to Spider-Man: Brand New Day as the highest-grossing movie of the year.
The Odyssey was the first movie shot entirely in IMAX cameras, and was shown in a number of different formats while in theaters. The digital release will have a 1.78:1 (16:9) aspect ratio to approximate the original IMAX format that isn’t natively supported on digital media platforms.
If you weren’t able to make it to the theaters, or just want to relive that specific experience, keep an eye out for more IMAX showings coming this December. Otherwise, your best bet is picking up the 4K disc edition. The 4K steelbook is currently sold out, but standard 4K, Blu-ray, and DVD releases are still available. These are also out on November 17, the first 'full day' the movie will be available on digital.
The Odyssey streaming release date
As a Universal release, The Odyssey will eventually stream on Peacock. Recent Universal releases have come to streaming around three months after their initial release date, which would have put The Odyssey’s streaming release date about a month ago. Like the delayed digital release, Universal is likely holding off on the streaming release to promote the digital and home video releases for a couple more months.
Do you prefer to see movies in theaters or wait until you can stream them at home?

item.title: Not content with plaguing your phone's lock screen, Duo the Duolingo owl is next set to appear in Pokémon Go.
item.description:
Not content with plaguing your phone's lock screen, Duo the Duolingo owl is next set to appear in Pokémon Go.
A crossover between the two hugely-popular smartphone apps has been announced, unlocking bonuses for players in both experiences. (Sadly, no, you won't be able to trap Duo in a Pokéball forever.)
The fun begins on November 17, when a time-limited event begins in Duolingo that requires you to complete at least one language lesson on seven separate days. This will then unlock a series of Pokémon-themed outfits for your Duolingo profile.
Completing all of that will also grant a promo code for Pokémon Go, unlocking timed research that awards Pokémon such as Pikachu and regional exclusive Chatot with a unique Duolingo background. It's rather cute — even if it does feature more of Duo the owl, too.
Pokemon Go Snapshot: Instructions and Photobombs
Why is all of this happening? While Pokémon Go has featured sponsored cosmetic items in the past, the game rarely offers this level of collaboration, and particularly not with another smartphone app. Still, earlier this year, the game also partnered with LEGO to offer similar bonus gameplay, centered around LEGO stores.
More prescient, perhaps, is the rollout of a new feature within Pokémon Go that will allow players to view the name of their creatures in multiple languages for the first time. While Pikachu is known as Pikachu the world over, other species have some very different names on foreign shores. (Snorlax is "Relaxo" in German, for example.)
And finally, in other Pokémon Go collaboration news, the creature catching app will soon feature a crossover with Crocs, the shoe brand that already offers a range of Pokémon clogs. All players can now unlock a virtual pair of Pikachu shoes by entering the promo code "POKEMONGOxCROCSxELECTRIFYING". Owners of the real-life Gengar and Jigglypuff shoes, meanwhile, will get codes for similar virtual versions of their own footwear.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Marvel Studios has revealed the release date for its Spider-Man: Brand New Day re-release, promising to bring new footage "and a couple more surprises" to theaters this December.
item.description:
Marvel Studios has revealed the release date for its Spider-Man: Brand New Day re-release, promising to bring new footage "and a couple more surprises" to theaters this December.
The official Spider-Man X/Twitter account confirmed plans to bring Peter Parker's (Tom Holland) first run-in with Jean Grey (Sadie Sink) back to moviegoers when the re-release arrives December 4, 2026. That means we're just a few weeks away from its premiere, with the full post teasing that this version of the movie is "an extended cut featuring new scenes and a couple more surprises."
Tickets go on sale this Thursday, November 19. Hope you're not busy!
As reported by Deadline earlier this year, Sony had plans to bring Spider-Man: Brand New Day back to theaters just months after the MCU movie's original premiere shattered records. Officially titled Spider-Man: Brand New Brand New Day, the outlet reported today that the plan is still for at least some of that new footage to include a cut scene featuring Rosario Dawson as her Defenders-era character, Night Nurse.
Even if you've had your fill of Holland's web-swinging antics for the year, Disney, Marvel, and Sony definitely know what they're doing when it comes to convincing MCU fans for a second round of their movies. Avengers: Doomsday will premiere just two weeks after Spidey returns. Although the December re-release may not be quite as likely to include any tie-in teaser footage like September's Avengers: Endgame Encore, Marvel fans will probably show up just to make sure, especially considering that "couple more surprises" tease.
There's also the fact that the wait for Avengers: Doomsday has already been quite long. Marvel has refrained from saying or showing too much about the film's actual plot, making that early December window a nice opportunity to capitalize on the hype and move Spider-Man's box-office needle just a little more.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day - Our Biggest Burning Questions
Spider-Man: Brand New Day premiered July 31, 2026, and was immediately a box office hit. It finally arrived on digital October 6 after grossing more than $2.5 billion worldwide, securing its place as one of the highest-grossing movies of all time.
IGN gave it a 7/10 review. At the time, we said it "effectively refocuses on the most reliable pillars of the webslinger: battling inner turmoil, swinging around NYC saving the day, and looking cool while doing so.

item.title: George Lazenby, who formerly portrayed James Bond, is giving Robert Pattinson some sage advice after the Batman actor scored the historic and highly coveted role.
item.description:
George Lazenby, who formerly portrayed James Bond, is giving Robert Pattinson some sage advice after the Batman actor scored the historic and highly coveted role.
After a lengthy and secretive casting process stacked with some of Britain’s greatest actors, Robert Pattinson was officially revealed as the next James Bond on November 16, 2026. This marks the latest in a string of high-profile parts Pattinson has played lately, which include Batman, Chris Hansen in Primetime, Antinous in Nolan’s Odyssey, and Scytale in Dune: Part Three.
It’s safe to say that Pattinson is no stranger to being the face of a franchise, what with his experience playing Edward Cullen in the Twilight saga and Batman in Matt Reeves’ take on the caped crusader. But James Bond is a different beast entirely, as fans’ reactions to this latest news have already proven this fact.
Luckily, he’s not alone. A slew of other actors have taken up the 007 mantle before him, including Lazenby, who portrayed the character in 1969's On Her Majesty’s Secret Service. Lazenby took the opportunity to give Pattinson some useful tips before he steps into M16.
“I hear they've announced the new James Bond,” Lazenby wrote in a post shared on social media. “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you'll have [a] ‘This never happened to the other fella!’ moment. All the best, mate, George xx.”
It’s safe to say Pattinson is already having one of those moments, given the energetic opinions we’ve seen on social media already. Many fans are ecstatic about him being cast as Bond, given his extensive filmography playing the tortured hero; others, however, aren’t so sure that he’s a good fit, while others are joking that he’s being too “greedy” by taking up all the best roles in Hollywood.
I hear they've announced the new James Bond @007... Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you'll have "this never happened to the other fella" moment. All the best mate, George xx https://t.co/r0kASTyp35
It’s certainly been quite a year for Pattinson, who’s had a nice few films that have dominated the box office this year. He, along with Tom Holland and Zendaya, is one of the most recognizable faces in the business right now — and it proves how far he’s come from his days as Edward Cullen.
In fact, Pattinson was apparently so coveted for Bond that he was reportedly offered a more lucrative contract for fewer films than other actors in the running, which included Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, and Nicholas Hoult.
For now, we’ll just have to wait and see what Pattinson’s Bond has to offer. In the meantime, you can look forward to watching him in Dune: Part Three this December.

item.title: Subway is getting on the GTA 6 hype train with a sandwich themed after the highly anticipated game.
item.description:
Subway is getting on the GTA 6 hype train with a sandwich themed after the highly anticipated game.
The sandwich chain announced today that it is giving its Miami-exclusive Cubano Pulled Pork Melt a GTA 6 "reskin" in time for the new game. The sandwich is being renamed the Vice City Cubano and, as noted, is only available in the city of Miami. The sandwich comes either as a six-inch or footlong sub and features hardwood-smoked pulled pork, black forest ham, melted provolone, pickles, and mustard on freshly baked artisan Italian bread.
Subway confirmed that the sandwich will be available both in-store and for delivery for those who don't plan to leave their couch when GTA 6 is released. You can see an image of it below.
Subway isn't the only fast food place getting in on on the GTA 6 hype. Popeyes is also releasing a Vice City-themed chicken sandwich that it calls "Spice City." It will be available for one week starting November 19 and is available at participating locations for in-store pick up or delivery. Finally, there are also a bunch of Miami-based dining options and stores that have officially teamed up with Rockstar to provide themed meals and drinks based on GTA. The most notable of the bunch is a partnership with Skinny Louie, a burger chain based out of Florida.
The chain has been turned into Burger Shot, a fast food joint prominently featured in the GTA franchise. The menu, uniforms, packaging, and signange for Skinny Louie has been completely refitted with Burger Shot branding, which will remain in place until the end of the year. Rockstar's marketing power has reached unprecedented levels, even prompting other places that don't have a partnership in place to try and ride the hype waves.
GTA 6 will release this Thursday for Xbox Series X|S and PS5. Players can pre-load the game right now and they absolutely should, as the game is a whopping 210 GBs.

item.title: The UK’s National Health Service is giving players advice to help them avoid straining their hands once GTA 6 finally releases on November 19.
item.description:
The UK’s National Health Service is giving players advice to help them avoid straining their hands once GTA 6 finally releases on November 19.
The service’s humorous PSA was posted to Instagram on November 16, just three days before Rockstar’s highly anticipated game launches. The post includes several photos taken by the NHS’s social media manager, whose hand has been wrapped up tight in a cast.
The poor employee explained that they underwent surgery to “remove a lump” from their hand, which they said is particularly “bad timing” due to GTA 6’s imminent release. To help others avoid injuring themselves and being unable to play, they shared some tips to keep your ligaments in tip-top shape.
For starters, the NHS is urging players to “try and take regular breaks.” This helps avoid eye strain, and getting up from your gaming chair or sofa every couple of hours is good for circulation, relieving muscle stiffness, and providing mental clarity. (That’s right — you might actually play better if you take regular breaks.)
The NHS’s post was particularly concerned with RSI, or repetitive strain injury, which it described as “pain that can be caused by repeated movement of part of the body, such as hands and fingers.”
RSI can happen for a number of reasons; sports like tennis or golfing can be culprits, as can jobs like hairdressing (using scissors and other tools), working an assembly line, and even typing at your computer.
GTA 6 Dynamic Weather Screenshots
While RSI is a general umbrella term for these types of injuries, carpal tunnel is a more specific condition that falls under the RSI label. Gamers are prone to this type of strain, due to pressing buttons quickly and repetitively, moving a joystick back and forth, and gripping one’s controller or mouse tightly while playing.
While a repetitive strain injury might legitimately be something you could call out of work for, you might have a hard time getting the time off, given how many players are already planning on taking time off from their jobs to roam around Vice City. There's already been a 17% increase in time-off requests from employees for November 19, and even world governments like Germany and Australia are talking about the game’s upcoming impact on the workforce.
In fact, estimates show that GTA 6 is likely to drain $1 billion from the US economy, since so many people will be staying at home to play on November 19. Some companies are getting a jump on the amount of ‘sick’ employees they’ll likely have by offering the time off ahead of time, with tech giant Logitech giving staff the option to take personal days for major video game releases. Just remember to take regular breaks — Vice City will be just fine without you for a few moments.

item.title: Rockstar has revealed a new batch of GTA 6 screenshots – and even a Weather Channel forecast – showcasing Leonida's dynamic weather.
item.description:
Rockstar has revealed a new batch of GTA 6 screenshots – and even a Weather Channel forecast – showcasing Leonida's dynamic weather.
The 13-year wait for a proper return to Vice City is almost over, but with just days to go until launch, no one had any idea what to expect from the week. Would more details leak? Would Rockstar reveal more gameplay details? Would we get more gameplay footage? Either way, it's probably safe to say no one was expecting to check the forecast to find out the latest on GTA 6.
The Weather Channel struck when it published a series of screenshots showing Vice City covered in everything from torrential downpours to ocean fog. We even get a true-to-life breakdown of what we're seeing here, giving would-be Leonida citizens a chance to prep before the storm hits.
Heavy rain is kicking up a lot of moisture making visibility poor in many places in the Keys, luckily the local authorities have installed reflectors in some of the roads to help driving (better get your headlights fixed at Coastal Auto Care) https://t.co/tpCfXirjV0
"Grand Theft Auto VI takes place in Leonida – a fictional world inspired by modern-day Florida, a landscape with one of the most unpredictable weather systems in the US," Rockstar VP of art: light and rendering Owen Shepherd said. "To match the fidelity of all aspects of what is the deepest, most immersive take on the Grand Theft Auto series yet, we had to completely reimagine our in-game weather systems to feel more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic. Weather can range with everything from clear blue skies to towering vertiginous cumulonimbus clouds, grounding players in a world through weather we hope Florida locals – and new visitors to Leonida – can appreciate."
Rockstar confirmed it had developed an "advanced" weather system when speaking to Game Informer in September. Another update that arrived shortly afterward revealed that Vice City could, in fact, be hit by simulated tropical storms and hurricanes. At the time, these were said to bring "heavy clouds, strong winds, dense atmospherics, and a lot of rain." That means more than simple visual changes as Leonida is overrun by Mother Nature.
These early details promised something a little more intense than the occasional shower, and now, we have our first look at what that might actually look like. While there's a lot of variety here, there's no reason to believe these six screenshots represent everything the skies of Leonida have to offer.
GTA 6 Dynamic Weather Screenshots
GTA 6 finally launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, 2026. It's a long time coming, with only a little bit more waiting to go. Luckily, we've got plenty to keep you busy. For a better look at the Grand Theft Auto series' history of Easter Eggs, click here. You can also click here if you'd like to take a peek into how Rockstar pulls from real life to make its games feel realistic, and if you're interested in how the top content creators are prepping for launch, click here. Oh, and if you need an excuse to stay home this Thursday, Xbox (kind of) has you covered.

item.title: Werwulf director Robert Eggers revealed to IGN that Robert Pattinson was watching his upcoming horror movie when the news of his casting as the next James Bond was announced today.
item.description:
Robert Pattinson was watching an upcoming horror movie when the news of his casting as the next James Bond was announced today.
IGN knows this thanks to filmmaker Robert Eggers, who directed Pattinson in The Lighthouse and just so happened to be at IGN’s Los Angeles studio today to do an interview about his next movie, Werwulf.
When I jokingly asked Eggers if he ever thought while watching Pattinson kill that seagull in The Lighthouse, “There goes the next James Bond,” he chuckled and responded:
“No, but I’m not surprised that it panned out the way that it did. And also, crazily enough, he was watching a screening of Werwulf when the news broke. And I was just texting with him about it this morning.”
So what did Pattinson think of Werwulf? “Oh, he loved it, of course,” Eggers responded with a grin.

Pattinson won the highly coveted role of James Bond after competing against the likes of Nicholas Hoult, Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, and Josh O’Connor.

item.title: World of Warcraft Forever has now been out for a couple of weeks, and it's had a remarkably smooth launch. But now that players are starting to get to high enough levels to engage with dungeons, Blizzard is trying to nail down exactly how dungeons should reward players.
item.description:
World of Warcraft Forever has now been out for a couple of weeks, and it's had a remarkably smooth launch. But now that players are starting to level up enough to engage with dungeons, Blizzard is trying to nail down exactly how dungeons should reward players.
Over the weekend, Blizzard pushed out a November 13 hotfix that made it so if there's any player in a group that's too high of a level to earn experience from monsters, no one in that group gets experience. The goal seems to be to get rid of boosting, where one high-level player can carry a group of players through dungeons to level them up quickly. But that solution backfired.
The problem is that in a lot of Forever's dungeons, there's a wide level range, so players on the high end of that range ended up accidentally nullifying everyone else's experience in the dungeon. That even happened to me on Saturday when trying to run Excavation Site with a level 37 player in my group.
World of Warcraft: Forever Screenshots
The next day, Blizzard admitted that hotfix went too far. On the WoW Forever forums, community manager Kaivax posted, saying, "Yesterday, we updated dungeon play so that experience granted by an enemy in an instance is nullified if a high level player is in the group and enemy is trivial to that player. For some dungeons, the new restriction missed the mark because of the overall level range of the enemies in the dungeon."
Instead, Blizzard changed the way the restriction works. Rather than basing it on whether or not an enemy is "trivial" to any of the players, there's now a flat level difference restriction on experience. As Kaivax puts it, "We’ve just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so that the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies."
For those who are just trying to do dungeons as they naturally come up while questing, the latest update should completely fix the issue, while also preventing boosters from powering people through the game. After all, Blizzard is dead-set on encouraging players to level out in the world, and is apparently not afraid of using some heavy-handed tactics to do so.
This also isn’t the first time that Blizzard has needed to adjust dungeon experience. Back when the WoW Forever beta first opened, the company severely limited the amount of XP you get from dungeons, only to buff it last week – even if it’s still far below what you’d earn in Classic. Blizzard has also changed the way gold is earned, in order to stop people from feeling like they had to hoard quest turn-ins for when they hit max level.

item.title: Pro wrestler Austin Creed went viral over the weekend for pulling off an iconic fighting game move in real life, hitting his opponent with an explosive Shoryuken in a viral moment that took social media by storm.
item.description:
Pro wrestler Austin Creed went viral over the weekend for pulling off an iconic fighting game move in real life, hitting his opponent with an explosive Shoryuken in a viral moment that took social media by storm.
Creed, alongside Kofi Kingston and Swerve Strickland, put on a stunning performance at AEW’s Full Gear event on Saturday, November 14. The trio took on Brody King, Hangman Page, and the masked Bandido for a 3v3 brawl that saw a number of props and weapons used in the fight, which are allowed by Texas Death Match rules.
One of these props was a Nintendo Power Glove, an old-school accessory for the Nintendo Entertainment System that was first released in 1989. Of course, being a pro wrestling match, this particular Power Glove had special powers that allowed its wearer to pull off some especially brutal moves.
Wake up ➡️⬇️↘️+👊🏾 https://t.co/lgJpD6oWy4
During his turn with King, Creed pulled the Power Glove out of a bag and slipped it on — but he took a tad too long, getting whacked in the head and sent to his knees. King smacked him a second time, seemingly outdoing his rival before Creed suddenly stood and hit him with a Shoryuken, his fist exploding in sparks and sending King flying backwards.
The moment went viral within wrestling circles and the fighting game community. Players wasted no time joking about Creed’s “wakeup DP” and “reversal,” with legendary pro player Justin Wong comparing the move to Daigo Umehara’s famed “Umeshoryus.”
To explain these terms to non-fighting gamers, a ‘DP’ refers to a Dragon Punch, which is a category of uppercut-style special move. ‘Wakeup’ is the moment that a player’s character recovers after being knocked down, while a ‘reversal’ refers to a player successfully executing a move and striking the opposing character as soon as possible after being hit. In essence, Creed hit King with a reversal DP on wakeup — a move that King probably should have seen coming.
Street Fighter Images
“Lmao he just stayed still without blocking on his wakeup, deserved to get hit by reversal DP,” prominent fighting game YouTuber Rooflemonger joked.
“This is the coldest thing I've seen in the ring in over two decades,” game artist CartelDel remarked.
“Totally invincible on frames 1-8,” another teased.
Creed is one of several pro wrestlers who have referenced fighting games in the ring; Kenny Omega famously uses moves like Street Fighter 5’s V-Trigger against his opponents, and even contributed to Alex’s moveset for Street Fighter 6. Cody Rhodes, who famously portrayed Guile in the 2026 Street Fighter movie, also showed up to WWE Summer Slam in full Guile attire — including the character’s iconic flat-top hairstyle.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement.
item.description:
Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement.
The latest turn in the tech giant's whirlwind week arrived yesterday, when the Financial Times reported that the company's ex-boss had supported efforts from his friends in Silicon Valley to see him brought back into the fold. One source said these allies had assembled a "war room" to lay the foundation for his return, but it now seems those efforts may have been for naught.
The Nvidia board of directors is not considering reinstating Huang as CEO after he resigned from his position Thursday, November 12, one source told CNBC. Instead, company leadership is focused on the ongoing investigation launched after Huang confirmed he had an affair with a woman whom members of the U.S. government believed to be a Chinese spy on November 8.
The report states Nvidia hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to look into his relationship with the individual and how it may have compromised company secrets and/or national security. A message from the board added it had "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised" when announcing the investigation last week.
One of the supposed goals of Huang's secret war room of Silicon Valley supporters was to gain White House support for the reinstatement – and it's a plan that seems to have panned out. U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters today (via Bloomberg) that he "would not mind" seeing the embattled tech leader return.
"I would not mind. I would not mind that," he said. "I threw out the name of Tim Cook, but I would say that Jensen's reinstatement… I think he learned a big lesson. I guess maybe one lesson's more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that."
Nvidia GeForce RTX 30-Series Reveal
Huang and Nvidia are now trying to pick up the pieces after the investigation began last week. The story so far has seen tech billionaire Elon Musk publicly back Huang, with some Nvidia employees saying they'd like him reinstated, too. Additional reports have said the former CEO had additional affairs with not one but two of his subordinates.
Photo by Nadja Wohlleben/Getty Images.

item.title: Even if you've been under a rock all year, it's hard to ignore the massive RAM crisis that's been going on since late 2025. And, while prices likely won't improve, it does seem like there's a small possibility that the three major RAM manufacturers might face some accountability.
item.description:
Even if you've been under a rock all year, it's hard to ignore the massive RAM crisis that's been going on since late 2025. And while prices likely won't improve, it does seem like there's a small possibility that the three major RAM manufacturers might face some accountability.
A class action lawsuit accusing Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung of colluding to fix the price of RAM while simultaneously scaling back production was filed back in June. This kind of case will likely take years to go through the system. But the RAM companies filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that each company made "rational choices consistent with their own independent self interest" and that the case was just a "rerun" of a similar case from 2022. But on Friday, Judge Noël Wise denied the motion.
Wise's order references the previous case, which was dismissed, saying, "During the hearing, Defendants quoted the late Honorable Judge Posner who famously wrote, '[c]ompetitors in concentrated markets watch each other like hawks.'" But then added, "But Plaintiffs’ allegations go beyond hawks watching each other; their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do."
Steam Machine – Hands On Photos
Now, before you go and celebrate that RAM prices are going to come crashing down, this order simply means that the case will move forward – the fight isn't over yet. This class action lawsuit will probably be moving through the courts for a couple years before any final decision is made.
While the previous 2022 class action was dismissed, the three companies named in this lawsuit do have a history of working together to manipulate the RAM market. All the way back in 2002, the U.S. Department of Justice investigated a "criminal cartel" made up of Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron in order to fix prices. That investigation ended in jail time for a Samsung executive, along with a $300 million fine for Samsung and a $185 million fine for SK Hynix.
If anything, though, the RAM market is worse for consumers than either of the two times that the three RAM companies have been accused of price fixing. According to the order, the last class action came after memory prices spiked by 165% in 2018. But compared to 2026, that's nothing. The order says, "In sum, Plaintiffs allege a 697% price increase for conventional DRAM over an eighteen-month period." Looking at RAM kits on Amazon, it's hard to deny that number.
Only time will tell how this lawsuit will play out, but no matter what happens, it doesn't seem like RAM prices are going to improve any time soon. Samsung told investors during its latest earnings call that "AI-driven demand [is] likely to further tighten supply shortages" next year. That was after all three memory manufacturers reported selling through their 2027 manufacturing capacity all the way back in August 2026. It's no wonder that Xbox Project Helix is rumored to hit $1,800.
Has the RAM crisis stopped you from upgrading or buying a PC?

item.title: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond, which means there is no shortage of opinions flying around the internet about this news.
item.description:
Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond, which means there's no shortage of opinions flying around the internet about this news.
It was confirmed today that Robert Pattinson has been cast as James Bond, with reports saying his deal was squared away as recently as yesterday. Pattinson's casting was reportedly last-minute, as the producers have been working through an array of actors for Bond all year long. Pattinson only submitted himself for the part a few weeks ago when filming on The Batman Part 2 briefly paused. As a result, it shook up the group of finalists, which reportedly included names like Jack Lowden and Callum Turner.
With Pattinson stealing the gig with a buzzer-beater screen test and snagging a lucrative deal, it's no surprise that reactions have been animated, to say the least. The biggest takeaway for many is that Pattinson is playing both Bond and Batman, seemingly at the same time. Some joked that this is rather greedy of him, since he's an extremely accomplished actor and is hogging up some of the best parts.
The Next James Bonds Who Never Played 007
"Yo, I'm actually sick bro; that motherf**ker is gonna finish with a top 5 filmography ever," joked one fan.
"Being both Batman and James Bond, this is the greed they talk about in the Bible," said another.
Others think this may be a sign that his days as Batman are coming to an end. Of course, DC Studios bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran were just ousted from the company and replaced by a newer, cheaper alternative. It seems like Skydance may want to save on costs and also make more accessible movies, and it's unclear if the highly-expensive, dark, gritty Matt Reeves-directed Batman films will allow for that. It may be feasible to complete a trilogy if Reeves can get a third movie turned around quickly, but it took five years between the first two movies, and the sequel has experienced some setbacks, as well.
"He’s done as Batman after Part II, obviously," suggested an observer.
Although it's not impossible for an actor to do multiple movies in a year or in quick succession, Batman and Bond are extremely physical roles that demand a lot from an actor. Depending on schedules, it means Pattinson would have to constantly stay in tip-top shape, and he may not have time to do smaller films like he did with Primetime and The Drama this year.
The Batman Part 2 started shooting in late May or early June, and is expected to continue filming into early 2027. A Bond film has a similar extended schedule that also takes actors around the globe, limiting opportunities to do other projects. Maybe Pattinson will find a way to juggle both roles if DC wants a third installment, but the jury is out.
Although Pattinson's casting has been met with a lot of hype, others aren't as sold, given that he's become known for taking weirder roles. He's also been exposed to the audience a lot in the last year.
The Top 10 Robert Pattinson Movies
"Love Pattinson, but c'mon man, y'all have to cast unknown actors for some stuff," said a user on X. "I don’t see him fitting Bond.
"I just don’t see it," said another user. "Looks more like a villain than Bond"
Ultimately, though, Pattinson's casting as Bond is being met with a lot more enthusiasm than his initial casting announcement for Batman was. Although he'd turned in strong performances in films like Good Time before Batman, he was best known for being a sparkly, moody vampire in Twilight. For some, that didn't jive with their idea of Batman. Since then, he has been in a number of respected films that have reached wider audiences, including The Odyssey and soon-to-be Dune Part 3.
There's currently no release date for Pattinson's first Bond outing, though some expect it will release in 2028 with a 2027 shoot date in mind. Director Denis Villeneuve will likely be badgered with questions about the project when promoting Dune 3 in the next month, so we may get some more ideas of what to expect soon.

item.title: A 13-year-old Tekken player went viral over the weekend for beating a seasoned pro in a competitive tournament — all while boasting a hairstyle that looked just like Kazuya Mishima’s.
item.description:
A 13-year-old Tekken player went viral over the weekend for beating a seasoned pro in a competitive tournament — all while boasting a hairstyle that looked just like Kazuya Mishima’s.
Thaiger Uppercut (TGU) is a major fighting game tournament that takes place in Thailand each fall. It’s known for drawing some of the best talent across multiple titles from around the world, with established players flocking to the competition for fame, glory, and of course, prize money.
This year, however, an unexpected combatant emerged: 13-year-old Martinski, a Tekken player from the Philippines, left audiences stunned after taking out Pinya, a well-known Japanese Tekken pro who has been competing at a top level since the days of Tekken 7.
HUGE round in pools.📺 https://t.co/10vkbWvgVE // #TEKKEN8 #TGU2026 https://t.co/TlC3imwNAD
Martinski beat Pinya 2-0 in a stunning show of strength, knocking his opponent to the losers’ bracket. However, it wasn’t just the absurd talent he displayed at such a young age that made him go viral within the fighting game community; he also styled his hair to look like Kazuya Mishima, the Tekken series’ former protagonist-turned-antagonist.
In fact, Martinski made it to the Top 48 — a solid feat for a player of any caliber, but an especially impressive achievement for one so young. Looking at Start.gg, the 13-year-old competitor finished in 25th place out of 187 other players,
Over on X/Twitter, Martinski spoke about his results, saying he was “proud of this run and grateful for the experience” and that “there's always something to take away from every tournament.”
@ELITE_Martinski IS INSANE AT TEKKEN 8 AND ONLY 13 YEARS OLD.CONGRATULATIONS FOR MAKING IT INTO TOP 48 AT TGU 🇹🇭 https://t.co/D9x1PTxUKN
Martinski also competed in a 3v3 teams bracket under the name ‘Martinski’s Magic Light Team.’ The group finished 9th out of 24 total teams.
Martinski’s performance at TGU highlights a growing trend within the fighting game community; young players are becoming increasingly successful in tournaments, particularly where Tekken 8 and Street Fighter 6 are concerned.
For example, 16-year-old Neia stunned audiences after making it to the Top 24 for Tekken 8 at Evo France, one of the most stacked tournaments of the season. She even beat established pros Hakim ‘Skywalker’ Touré and Jonathan ‘Tibetano’ Medina to get there, and has been a rising star in the scene ever since then.
And in Street Fighter 6, 17-year-old Chilean player Blaz recently helped his team win the Street Fighter League Americas Finals — but he’s been knocking heads since he was just 15, and even got second place at Capcom Cup 11 a few months after his 16th birthday. Another young Chilean talent, Craime, made the Top 8 at Evo Las Vegas this year at 15 years old, but has been competing in tournaments since he was 13. He famously won the Esports World Cup for Street Fighter 6 earlier this year, cementing his status as a major threat for the competition.
I got the chance to interview Blaz after his monumental victory with team 2Game after the SFL Americas Finals last weekend, where he explained why modern games like Street Fighter 6 attract younger players and why LATAM is such a strong region right now.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Magic: The Gathering Star Trek is just a couple weeks old at this point, but lead designer Mark Rosewater has confirmed that there are no plans for additional Star Trek sets.
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering Star Trek is just a couple weeks old at this point, but head designer Mark Rosewater has confirmed that there are no plans for additional Star Trek sets.
Star Trek was the latest MTG Universes Beyond set, which boasts 497 cards from across all of the franchise's history. It's a similar approach to how Wizards of the Coast handled Marvel Superheroes earlier this year, which also covered a wide swatch of the comics franchise. But, while Marvel has a set right around the corner in April 2027 with Darkhold Destiny, WotC will not be returning to the final frontier.
Rosewater replied to a question on his Tumblr, speculating on where future Star Trek Magic sets may go, saying flat-out that "there are no current plans for future Star Trek sets." The question Rosewater was responding to came from user yodasws and called out Darkhold Destiny specifically and speculated that the next Star Trek set could cover something like the Dominion War, which would focus on a huge portion of Deep Space 9. Or, even more specifically, a set based in the Delta Quadrant.
Magic the Gathering: Star Trek – IGN Exclusive Card Reveals
In the same post, Rosewater also denied that Marvel Superheroes was a generic Marvel set, saying, "Marvel Super Heroes wasn’t generic. It was what we called 'Avengers plus,' it was a specific slice of the property."
Rather than focusing on one big pre-existing Marvel story arc, Darkhold Destiny is Wizards of the Coast taking Marvel's IP and creating their own story out of it. WotC worked alongside Marvel to create something entirely new, rather than paying homage to a pre-existing storyline like yodasws speculated.
When Darkhold Destiny comes out next year, it’ll be the third Marvel set to come to Magic: The Gathering, and there are likely going to be many more over the next few years. After all, Marvel’s Spider-Man and Marvel Superheroes each had their own Infinity Stone, the Soul Stone, and Mind Stone, respectively... and there are still six more to go.
But while there won’t be any more Star Trek sets coming to Magic, there are plenty of valuable cards to collect. It turns out that even Brandon Sanderson is a huge fan.

item.title: Shadow Recompiled is an unofficial PC port of the 2005 Sonic spinoff, now with achievements and more.
item.description:
There is no shortage of classic games getting so-called "unofficial PC ports" right now. Previously, these recompilation projects were few and far between because they take a ridiculous amount of time to make. But now, with many modders using generative AI to help them code, they're being pumped out so fast it's hard to keep up.
The problem with this is that not everyone wants to play a game that's vibecoded, either for ethical reasons or due to concerns over the quality. After all, recompiled games are supposed to feel like you are playing a game natively on PC, so expectations are high.
Thankfully, the Sonic community has never shied away from a challenge. Previously, Sonic Unleashed was recompiled and released to play on PC. As long as you could provide your own game files (i.e., prove that you owned the game legitimately on console), you could start playing on PC, with modern-day quality-of-life improvements.
Now, another Sonic game has gotten the same treatment. Or, rather, a Shadow game. Yes, I am of course talking about 2005's Shadow the Hedgehog, originally released for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and original Xbox.
Released as Shadow Recompiled, this project brings Shadow the Hedgehog to PC, and with modern comforts.
Shadow the Hedgehog (2005)RECOMPILED!Native PC port of the Xbox version (no emulator)Easy installer + PC options menuWidescreen / ultrawide supportHigh / unlocked FPS D3D12 & VulkanBloom overhaul + many QoL fixesAchievements Mod support (SA Mod Manager)NO VIBECODE/ AI https://t.co/Xt3U2ZsBAv
Specifically, this brings the Xbox release to PC. But rather than emulating an Xbox, it should run as if it was actually released on PC.
The benefit of these releases is that they can be easier for modders to work with. That means the devs have added a whole new options menu with FPS adjustments, fullscreen toggle, and V-sync, so it should look and run better than ever. There are also achievements and ultrawide monitor support.
As ever, you will have to provide the game files yourself. The devs tell players to do so from a copy of the game they have legally acquired themselves. But once you have that, you can download Shadow Recompiled and get stuck in. Better yet, thanks to mod support, we can expect more fan-made improvements down the line.

item.title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians showrunners explain how Christopher Nolan's blockbuster The Odyssey unexpectedly boosted the Disney+ series' viewership over the summer.
item.description:
A new season of Percy Jackson and the Olympians is coming to Disney+ in just a few days and the executive producers of the show are revealing that Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey just might have led to a ratings boost for the series over the summer.
I sat down with Percy Jackson showrunners Dan Shotz and Jonathan E. Steinberg at, where they revealed that Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster The Odyssey probably led to more people discovering Percy Jackson over the summer.
“We've heard that there was a huge boost in viewers during that period because everybody obviously was searching for The Odyssey,” EP and co-showrunner Dan Shotz told IGN at Lucca Comics & Games. “And anybody who didn't know about Sea of Monsters, [the second Percy Jackson book, which was the source material for the show’s second season,] found it. But it was kind of surreal, to be honest with you, to watch it.”
The second season of Percy Jackson and the Olympians sees the titular teenage hero take a distinctly Odyssey-like journey, complete with maritime adventures and mythical creatures like the cyclops Polyphemus, the monstrous Scylla and Charybdis, the witch Circe, and the tempting sirens, just like Matt Damon’s Odysseus in Christopher Nolan’s film.
Shotz said he’s enjoyed how the two opposing takes on Homer’s classic poem have led to some distinctly modern outcomes.
“My favorite thing is all the memes that are going around that are like, ‘It took Odysseus however many hundreds of years to do this and it took Percy seven days. So he did it a lot more efficiently,’” Shotz said. “It was weird to see all of these iconic things that we were able to play with and that [Nolan and his team] were playing with in there, and how they did it versus how we did it. So that part was really fun.”
For his part, Shotz’s fellow executive producer and showrunner Jonathan E. Steinberg said he’s excited for fans of Percy Jackson to see what comes after The Sea of Monsters arc as they dive into Season 3 of the show, based on Riordan’s novel The Titan’s Curse.
“The hardest thing to do was to figure out how to manage all of these new faces and old faces who are in new relationships and in new places emotionally and make them all as important as Season 1 or 2,” Steinberg said. “The way you're watching Percy (Walker Scobell), who was the new kid not that long ago, figure out how to be a little bit of an authority figure in this world. We've been very lucky to find people who have just kept adding to the palette of what this show can do.”
Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3 premieres November 20 on Disney+.

item.title: Actress and cult horror favorite Maika Monroe has confirmed that she won't return as FBI agent Lee Harker in the upcoming Longlegs sequel, although she's not quite ready to say goodbye to the character for good.
item.description:
Actress and cult horror favorite Maika Monroe has confirmed that she won't return as FBI agent Lee Harker in the upcoming Longlegs sequel, although she's not quite ready to say goodbye to the character for good.
Speaking to ScreenRant while promoting her latest horror movie, Victorian Psycho, Monroe was asked whether she'd be reprising her role in the follow-up to Oz Perkins' 2024 nerve-shredding nightmare.
"Lee Harker will not be in this one," Monroe confirmed, although her response wasn't entirely straightforward. The actress briefly trailed off with an intriguing "I'll just..." before reiterating that Harker wouldn't appear in the sequel.
However, Monroe added that she "would love to revisit that role," suggesting that while Harker won't be appearing in Longlegs 2, the door isn't necessarily closed on her returning further down the line. It's an interesting development, particularly given how the original movie ended.
Warning: Spoilers for Longlegs follow...
Harker survived her encounter with Nicolas Cage's deeply disturbing serial killer, but her story was hardly wrapped up neatly. After discovering the truth about her mother's involvement in Longlegs' Satanic murders, Harker was left facing the possibility that the evil she'd spent the movie investigating wasn't quite finished with her.
Of course, the bigger mystery surrounding Longlegs 2 is how Nicolas Cage is returning at all, considering his character rather definitively smashed his own face to pieces in the original movie.
Would you prefer a Longlegs sequel or prequel next?
